messages.author: ec1bc1bea8773650
messages.subject: Use of countXO or locateX0
parts:
Hello,
I work on BC2F4 lines. a qtl has been detected on a chromosome. I want to identify  individuals who have a recombination in this region of the qtl. For this I have selected 2 SNPs around the position of the QTL and I want to see where the recombination occurs. I tried to use locateX0 or countXO but the functions are not available for BCsFT, what may i do?
Also I want to check order of markers but checkAlleles or ripple don't work for this type cross. Do you have any suggestions ? thank you
Princia

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Use of countXO or locateX0
parts:
You could try treating it as an F2. I think locateXO and countXO could be the same for BC2F4 as for an F2.

I'm surprised ripple() doesn't work. What error are you getting?

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Use of countXO or locateX0
parts:
Following up on this: ripple() should work for your bc2f3 population.
locateXO() and countXO() will work if you change the cross to "f2".

    class(mycross)[1] <- "f2"
    xoloc <- locateXO(mycross)

In the next release of R/qtl, you'll be able to use locateXO and countXO without changing the cross type.
You can install that version with the remotes package:

    install.packages("remotes")
    remotes::install_github("kbroman/qtl")

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Re: Use of countXO or locateX0
parts:
I would stick with the physical order. For the likelihood analysis, a positive LOD score would indicate that the alternate order was better supported. Here, the physical order has the highest likelihood.

I would also include more markers in this analysis; ideally all of the markers on the chromosome. The surrounding markers provide important information.

karl

On Tuesday, November 1, 2022 at 8:20:55 PM UTC-5 princ...@gmail.com wrote:
here the following code and results:

mydata=est.rf(mydata)
plotRF(mydata)


checkAlleles(mydata)
Error in checkAlleles(mydata) :
  checkAlleles not available for cross type bcsft

class(mydata)[1]="f2"
checkAlleles(mydata)
No apparent problems

class(mydata)[1]="bcsft"

rip <- ripple(mydata, 1, 4)
summary(rip)

                       obligXO
Initial  1 2 3 4      42
1        1 4 3 2      41

mydata <- switch.order(mydata, 1, rip[2,])
rip <- ripple(mydata, 1, 2, method="likelihood",error.prob=0.001, verbose=FALSE)
summary(rip)

                         LOD  chrlen
Initial  1 2 3 4     0.0  1032.2
1        1 3 2 4    -1.7  1043.1

mydata=est.rf(mydata)
plotRF(mydata)

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Re :Re: [Rqtl-disc] Re: Use of countXO or locateX0
parts:
If you are focused on just marker order around the QTL, you might look at the function compareorder(), where you can focus on different permutations of some focused set of markers, rather than applying ripple to the entire chromosome.

    data(badorder)
    compareorder(badorder, chr=1, order=c(1:8,11,10,9,12))

karl
